# National Development Parallel Coordinates Dataset

## Overview
This dataset contains 30 countries spanning four World Bank income groups (High, Upper-Middle, Lower-Middle, Low) with seven development indicators, designed for a parallel coordinates visualization of multidimensional national profiles.

## Data Source

### national_development
Each record represents one country with the following fields:
- **country** (string): Country name
- **income_group** (string): World Bank income classification — one of High, Upper-Middle, Lower-Middle, Low
- **gdp_per_capita_usd** (numeric): GDP per capita in current USD, range ~380–87,720
- **hdi** (numeric): Human Development Index, range 0.394–0.961
- **freedom_index** (numeric): Freedom House aggregate score, 0–100 (100 = most free)
- **corruption_perceptions_index** (numeric): Transparency International CPI score, 0–100 (100 = least corrupt)
- **co2_emissions_per_capita_tons** (numeric): Annual CO₂ emissions in metric tons per capita, range 0.1–21.8
- **military_expenditure_pct_gdp** (numeric): Military spending as percentage of GDP, range 0.6–6.0
- **internet_penetration_pct** (numeric): Percentage of population using the internet, range 14–99

## Data Notes
- Values are approximate 2023 estimates compiled from World Bank, UNDP, Freedom House, Transparency International, IEA, SIPRI, and ITU.
- Income group assignments follow the World Bank July 2023 classification.
- Some values for conflict-affected states (e.g., Afghanistan) carry higher uncertainty.
- CO₂ figures are production-based and exclude land-use change emissions.

import json

import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame(raw["national_development"]["data"])

# Define axes and display properties

    ("gdp_per_capita_usd", "GDP per Capita (USD)", "$", True),
    ("hdi", "HDI", "", False),
    ("freedom_index", "Freedom Index", "", False),
    ("corruption_perceptions_index", "CPI Score", "", False),
    ("co2_emissions_per_capita_tons", "CO₂ per Capita (t)", "", False),
    ("military_expenditure_pct_gdp", "Military % GDP", "%", False),
    ("internet_penetration_pct", "Internet %", "%", False),
]

# Color palette - professional, data-dense style
income_order = ["High", "Upper-Middle", "Lower-Middle", "Low"]
colors = {
    "High": "#2166AC",           # deep blue
    "Upper-Middle": "#4DAF4A",   # green
    "Lower-Middle": "#FF7F00",   # orange
    "Low": "#D63384",            # magenta-red
}

# Normalize each axis to [0, 1] for plotting
norm_data = {}
tick_vals = {}
for col, label, unit, is_currency in axes:
    vals = df[col].values.astype(float)
    vmin, vmax = vals.min(), vals.max()
    margin = (vmax - vmin) * 0.05
    norm_data[col] = (vals - vmin) / (vmax - vmin) if vmax > vmin else np.zeros_like(vals)
    # Create 5 tick marks in original units
    tick_positions = np.linspace(0, 1, 5)
    tick_labels_vals = np.linspace(vmin, vmax, 5)
    if is_currency:
        tick_labels = [f"${int(v):,}" for v in tick_labels_vals]
    elif col == "hdi":
        tick_labels = [f"{v:.3f}" for v in tick_labels_vals]
    elif col == "co2_emissions_per_capita_tons":
        tick_labels = [f"{v:.1f}" for v in tick_labels_vals]
    elif col == "military_expenditure_pct_gdp":
        tick_labels = [f"{v:.1f}" for v in tick_labels_vals]
    else:
        tick_labels = [f"{int(v)}" for v in tick_labels_vals]
    tick_vals[col] = (tick_positions, tick_labels)

# Identify outliers for emphasis
# Outliers: countries far from their income group mean on any dimension
outlier_countries = set()
for col, *_ in axes:
    for ig in income_order:
        group_vals = df[df["income_group"] == ig][col]
        mean_val = group_vals.mean()
        std_val = group_vals.std()
        if std_val > 0:
            for idx, row in df[df["income_group"] == ig].iterrows():
                z = abs((row[col] - mean_val) / std_val)
                if z > 1.8:
                    outlier_countries.add(row["country"])

# Outlier profiles specifically called out:
# High-income with unusually high CO2: UAE, Saudi Arabia, Australia, US
# High-income with low freedom: Saudi Arabia, UAE, Singapore
# Upper-middle with low freedom: China, Russia, Thailand, Turkey
# Low-income with high military: Mali, Afghanistan, Chad, Uganda
extra_outliers = {"Saudi Arabia", "United Arab Emirates", "Singapore",
                  "China", "Russia", "Thailand", "Turkey",
                  "Mali", "Afghanistan", "Chad", "Uganda"}
outlier_countries = outlier_countries | extra_outliers

# --- Create figure ---
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(18, 9), dpi=150)

# Background
fig.patch.set_facecolor("#FAFAFA")
ax.set_facecolor("#FAFAFA")

n_axes = len(axes)
x_positions = np.arange(n_axes)

# Draw axis lines and ticks
for i, (col, label, unit, is_currency) in enumerate(axes):
    ax.axvline(x=i, color="#AAAAAA", linewidth=0.8, zorder=1)
    # Axis label at top
    ax.text(i, 1.08, label, ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=10.5,
            fontweight="bold", color="#333333", transform=ax.get_xaxis_transform())
    # Ticks
    tick_pos, tick_labs = tick_vals[col]
    for tp, tl in zip(tick_pos, tick_labs):
        ax.text(i, tp, tl, ha="center", va="center", fontsize=7.5, color="#555555",
                bbox=dict(boxstyle="round,pad=0.15", facecolor="#FAFAFA", edgecolor="none", alpha=0.9))

# Draw polylines — draw low-income first (background), high-income last (foreground)
# so high-income stands out
draw_order = ["Low", "Lower-Middle", "Upper-Middle", "High"]

for ig in draw_order:
    group_df = df[df["income_group"] == ig]

            zorder = 4
        else:

            alpha = 0.45

        # Label outlier countries

            for col_name, *_ in axes:

            max_dev = 0
            label_axis = 0
            for j, (col_name, *_ ) in enumerate(axes):
                dev = abs(row[col_name] - group_means[col_name])
                if dev > max_dev:
                    max_dev = dev
                    label_axis = j

            y_pos = norm_data[axes[label_axis][0]][row.name]
            # Offset labels to avoid overlap
            offset_x = 0.15 if j % 2 == 0 else -0.15
            ha = "left" if label_axis < n_axes - 1 else "right"

            # Smarter label placement
            if label_axis == 0:
                ha = "right"
                offset_x = -0.08
            elif label_axis == n_axes - 1:
                ha = "left"
                offset_x = 0.08
            else:
                ha = "left"
                offset_x = 0.08

            ax.annotate(row["country"],
                       xy=(label_axis, y_pos),
                       xytext=(offset_x * 3, 3),
                       textcoords="offset points",
                       fontsize=6.5, color=color, fontweight="bold", alpha=0.9,
                       ha=ha, va="bottom",
                       zorder=5,
                       arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-", color=color, alpha=0.4, lw=0.5))

# Highlight the Freedom-CPI region with a subtle bracket
# Draw a subtle shaded region between axes 2 and 3
ax.axvspan(2 - 0.3, 3 + 0.3, alpha=0.06, color="#888888", zorder=0)
ax.text(2.5, -0.12, "Freedom–CPI\nCluster Region", ha="center", va="top",
        fontsize=8, color="#666666", style="italic",
        transform=ax.get_xaxis_transform())

# Add crossover annotations for key nonlinear relationships
# GDP→HDI crossover: high GDP doesn't always mean highest HDI
ax.annotate("", xy=(1, 0.65), xytext=(0.5, 0.85),
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="->", color="#999999", lw=1, ls="--"))
ax.text(0.7, 0.78, "Nonlinear\ncrossover", fontsize=7, color="#777777",
        ha="center", style="italic", transform=ax.transData)

# CPI→CO2 crossover: low CPI (corrupt) can have varying CO2
ax.annotate("", xy=(4.5, 0.3), xytext=(3.5, 0.7),
            arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="->", color="#999999", lw=1, ls="--"))
ax.text(4.0, 0.55, "Sharp\ndivergence", fontsize=7, color="#777777",
        ha="center", style="italic", transform=ax.transData)

# Axis limits and formatting
ax.set_xlim(-0.5, n_axes - 0.5)
ax.set_ylim(-0.05, 1.05)
ax.set_xticks([])
ax.set_yticks([])

# Remove spines
for spine in ax.spines.values():
    spine.set_visible(False)

# Title
ax.set_title("National Development Profiles: Parallel Coordinates Across 7 Dimensions",
             fontsize=15, fontweight="bold", color="#222222", pad=30, loc="left")
ax.text(0, 1.14, "30 countries colored by World Bank income group  |  Outlier profiles labeled  |  Data: approximate 2023 estimates",
        fontsize=9, color="#666666", transform=ax.get_xaxis_transform(), ha="left")

# Legend
legend_elements = [
    Line2D([0], [0], color=colors["High"], linewidth=2.5, label="High Income"),
    Line2D([0], [0], color=colors["Upper-Middle"], linewidth=2.5, label="Upper-Middle Income"),
    Line2D([0], [0], color=colors["Lower-Middle"], linewidth=2.5, label="Lower-Middle Income"),
    Line2D([0], [0], color=colors["Low"], linewidth=2.5, label="Low Income"),
    Line2D([0], [0], color="#888888", linewidth=0.9, alpha=0.5, label="Non-outlier"),
    Line2D([0], [0], color="#888888", linewidth=1.8, alpha=0.85, label="Outlier profile"),
]
legend = ax.legend(handles=legend_elements, loc="lower right", fontsize=9,
                   frameon=True, facecolor="#FFFFFF", edgecolor="#CCCCCC",
                   title="Income Group", title_fontsize=10, ncol=2)
legend.get_title().set_color("#333333")

plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.02, 1, 0.98])
plt.savefig("/app/output/result.png", dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight",
